name: Aryaka
product_focus: Aryaka Unified SASE, SmartCONNECT, private core
evidence_summary: Aryaka sources evidence Unified SASE as-a-service, private global core network, SD-WAN, NGFW, SWG, IDPS, WAN optimisation and observability.
cost_model: Quote-based managed service; pricing normally depends on sites, bandwidth, regions, security stack and optimisation.
key_differentiators: Unified SASE delivered as a managed service from end to end, including the private global core network and WAN optimisation.
Strong story for global organisations needing predictable performance between regions without internet variability.
Embedded WAN optimisation differentiates from pure cloud-delivered SASE platforms.
best_fit_for: Global enterprises wanting SASE delivered as a fully managed service rather than as DIY platform plus tools.
Buyers who need consistent inter-regional performance for chatty applications.
Organisations preferring a vendor that owns the platform and the managed service rather than coordinating multiple parties.
watch_outs: Smaller PoP footprint and partner ecosystem than the hyperscale SASE vendors; coverage must match your geographic profile.
DIY/self-managed model has limited evidence; this is a managed-service-first proposition.
CASB and DLP capabilities have partial public evidence; depth should be confirmed in RFP.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Industry, region, organisation-size and pricing evidence was sourced on the same basis. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason. The value_tier field is a Netify assessment of relative cost position, not a supplier claim: most of this market publishes no price. Sources found and rejected are listed at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: AI Observe anomaly detection on the private core; AI Perform for application optimisation.

resilience.note: Owned Layer 2 core with 40+ PoPs and managed middle mile; built-in link and PoP failover.

profile.platform_architecture: Aryaka runs its own Layer 2 private core between 40+ PoPs with built-in WAN optimisation, delivering SD-WAN and application acceleration as a managed service. ANAP edges (or virtual equivalents) connect sites to the nearest PoP; the middle mile is Aryaka's, with deterministic latency that public-internet SASE clouds cannot guarantee. China connectivity is a long-standing speciality.
profile.security_sase: Aryaka Unified SASE adds cloud-delivered security at the PoPs: NGFW, SWG, ZTNA and CASB capabilities integrated with the network layer, plus partnerships for specialist depth. AI Observe provides anomaly detection across the estate. Security capability is credible and converging, with the network and acceleration heritage remaining the primary differentiation.
profile.service_support_channel: Aryaka is managed-service-first: co-managed and fully managed offers with 24x7 follow-the-sun operations and aggressive deployment timelines (sites in days). Last-mile procurement and management can be bundled. UK and EMEA presence is established direct and through partners.
profile.commercials_verdict: Subscription per site by bandwidth with the middle mile included, quote based; pricing reflects the private core. The Netify verdict: shortlist Aryaka for global estates with Asia or China exposure, application performance pain on long routes, or a desire to consume WAN and SASE as one managed service with deterministic performance. Regional UK-only estates rarely need the private core premium.

vendor_faqs.q: Why pay for Aryaka's private core instead of internet middle mile?
vendor_faqs.a: Deterministic latency and loss on long-haul routes: Frankfurt to Singapore or London to Shanghai behave consistently because traffic rides Aryaka's Layer 2 core with built-in optimisation, not best-effort internet peering.

vendor_faqs.q: How good is Aryaka for China connectivity?
vendor_faqs.a: It is one of the established answers: licensed in-country partnerships and PoPs give compliant, performant connectivity for foreign enterprises operating in China, an area where most SASE clouds struggle.

vendor_faqs.q: Is Aryaka DIY or managed only?
vendor_faqs.a: Managed-first with co-managed options: you keep policy visibility and change rights while Aryaka runs the platform and middle mile. Pure DIY is not the model; buyers wanting full self-operation should look at appliance-led vendors.

shortlist_summary: Aryaka deliver Unified SASE as a fully managed service end to end, and unlike most managed providers, they own the private global core network rather than relying on public internet paths for the underlay. Typically shortlisted by businesses needing a single end-to-end managed provider with a private backbone, particularly where WAN optimisation and fast global deployment are both requirements.
cost_note: Subscription per site with the private middle mile included; pricing reflects the owned core.
uk_basis: No UK HQ (US). UK PoP on the private core; managed-service delivery into the UK.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: Aryaka-managed: Leverage Aryaka and we take care as a single point of contact managed services provider.
f01_fully_managed_service.note: Aryaka positions a fully managed option in which it is the single point of contact. Corroborated by the managed Unified SASE page line "Fully, co-, and self-managed security and networking functions." and by Aryaka operating its own 24/7 NOC, orchestration and last mile management.

f03_co_managed_service.quote: Co-managed: Hand over some aspects to Aryaka or an Aryaka partner and keep others to yourself per your preference.
f03_co_managed_service.note: Explicit co-managed model in which the customer retains selected policy and change rights while Aryaka or an Aryaka partner runs the rest. A self-managed option is also offered on the same page.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.quote: Utilizes the Aryaka Network Management and Control (ANMC) system for scalable, multi-tenant automation and orchestration
f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: Multi-tenant orchestration is confirmed at platform level, the partner programme names Managed Service Providers and System Integrators as a partner category, and co-management can be delegated to an Aryaka partner. However I found no vendor statement about white-label or partner-branded portals, delegated administration roles or tenant templates on the partners page or elsewhere, so this falls short of the full definition.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: The Aryaka Smart Hands Service provides on-site and hands-on assistance for the configuration, activation, and implementation of the foundational Aryaka SD-WAN services at customer locations.
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: Two named professional services lines exist: Day 0 services covering "initial configuration, design and implementation of Aryaka security services" with a menu including "migration services to Aryaka security, integration services", and Smart Hands for on-site activation. No published evidence found for formal rollback plans or training curricula, so the grade rests on discovery, design, implementation and migration only.

f07_lifecycle_management.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. I checked the ANAP datasheet, the Services Description and Terms page and both the March 2024 and November 2025 PDF editions for hardware replacement, RMA, advance replacement, firmware upgrades, patching, warranty and end of life language and found none. The only lifecycle wording located was "MyAryaka customer portal always provides full visibility and control over the VM life cycle management" on the hosted VM firewall datasheet, which concerns a virtual appliance add-on rather than hardware lifecycle, and "Aryaka reserves the right to upgrade the Services and/or add additional functionality from time to time with or without notice" in the terms, which is a vendor right rather than a customer lifecycle commitment. Absence of a published statement is not proof the capability is missing.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: Aryaka provides truly global last mile services including wireline and 4G/5G wireless connectivity
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: 4G and 5G are confirmed as supported and procurable last mile transport. Graded partial rather than yes because the ANAP appliance datasheet contains no mention of LTE, 5G, cellular, SIM or modem, and the High Availability datasheet describes redundancy only as dual ISP links, so integrated modem, SIM management and signal monitoring are not evidenced in the sources reviewed.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.quote: Aryaka Secure Remote Access provides integrated, managed VPN as a service connecting users to the nearest Aryaka POP.
f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: The gateways are Aryaka's own infrastructure, not a resold third party's. Corroborated by "a global private network interconnected in a mesh service fabric of over 40 Points of Presence (PoPs) across the globe" and by the NGFW being hosted on the ANAP and on Aryaka's POP, so SaaS acceleration, remote access and security enforcement all run on vendor operated PoPs.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. The PoP locations page, the Global Connectivity datasheet, the Services Description and Terms page and the November 2025 terms PDF were all checked for dedicated PoP, private PoP, customer hosted PoP or sovereign deployment wording and none was found. Aryaka publishes only its own shared multi-tenant PoP estate. Absence of a statement is not proof the option does not exist.

f21_private_global_backbone.quote: Aryaka's private global network is a closed network in which data is transported through enterprise-grade encrypted tunnels
f21_private_global_backbone.note: Aryaka states the service "is based on a private core network delivering software-defined wide-area networking" interconnecting over 40 PoPs on six continents, so inter-region traffic rides a vendor controlled core rather than the public internet. This is control of a leased optical and IP core rather than proven ownership of physical fibre; no source reviewed states Aryaka owns the underlying fibre.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.quote: Operates 24x7x365 to maintain industry-leading SLAs for uptime, latency, jitter and packet loss globally.
f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: Aryaka publishes a full SLA document with per service uptime targets ("Uptime of 99.999%" for PrivateCore, NGFW-SWG, PrivateAccess and RemoteUser, and Internet Breakout), a target of "Packet Loss of less than 0.1%", per minute probing, monthly measurement and graduated service credits of 5, 10 and 20 percent of Link Service Fees. That is contractual rather than best effort.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.quote: Aryaka has built a dedicated security stack on top of our Software Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) architecture
f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: The NGFW-SWG is Aryaka authored and runs on both the ANAP and Aryaka POPs, with IPS, anti-malware, application control via inline CASB and DPI, and URL filtering that "Protects users from accessing malicious URLs using reputation scores for more than 32 billion URLs." Note that a separate optional SmartSecure Hosted VM Firewall Service is partner technology ("The first technology partner providing the NGFW functionality is Palo Alto Networks with its VM series of virtualized NGFWs.") and the Services Description and Terms references a Check Point EULA, so a partner_integrated firewall option exists alongside the native one. The integrated platform firewall itself is native.

f33_data_loss_prevention.quote: Aryaka Data Loss Prevention safeguards sensitive data with real-time monitoring and policy enforcement.
f33_data_loss_prevention.note: The Next-Gen DLP datasheet describes classification and inspection ("AI-powered natural language processing, contextual analysis", "named entry recognition (NER)", "Image Based Detection") across "data in motion, archived files, compressed files", with enforcement actions "Permit, Drop, Log Only, Redact, Masking & Skip" and alerting where "Security events (policy hits, IPS alerts) and asset data are presented in a common UI over MyAryaka". It is described as built into the Aryaka Unified SASE as a Service platform and requires the Aryaka Advanced Security tier. Formal exception approval workflow detail was not found.

f40_managed_service_assurance.quote: Aryaka operates its own 24/7 NOC (Network Operations Center) to manage, orchestrate, and monitor all traffic
f40_managed_service_assurance.note: The 24/7 NOC half of the definition is well evidenced: Aryaka runs its own NOCs "24x7x365 to maintain industry-leading SLAs for uptime, latency, jitter and packet loss globally", provides "24x7 proactive Link Monitoring and management of Customer's procured last mile links" and "24x7 health monitoring and handle incident management issues related to the ZTNA Gateways". Graded partial because the Services Description and Terms explicitly excludes a managed SOC from at least one offering: "managed SOC (Security Operation Center) are not part of the scope of the Managed Firewall Service offering, and Customer is solely responsible for these functions." No published evidence found for root cause analysis commitments or structured service review and change governance.

delivery_model.quote: Aryaka-managed: Leverage Aryaka and we take care as a single point of contact managed services provider.
delivery_model.note: Aryaka authors its own platform (ANAP appliance, ANMC orchestration, MyAryaka portal, its own security stack) and also operates it as a managed service with its own PoPs, private core and 24x7x365 NOCs. Both technology vendor and managed provider.

underlay_ownership.quote: Leverage our worldwide Tier-1 ISP partnerships and expertise in the procurement, deployment and monitoring of Last Mile Links
underlay_ownership.note: Core routing and the inter-PoP fabric are Aryaka's own: "Aryaka Global Connectivity is based on a private core network delivering software-defined wide-area networking" and Aryaka operates the PoPs and NOCs. Last mile is either resold by Aryaka from Tier-1 ISP partners ("Last Mile Service allows Customer to purchase last mile internet connection services like DIA, Broadband, Fixed Wire etc. from Aryaka") or procured by the customer and monitored by Aryaka under a Letter of Authorization. No source reviewed states Aryaka owns physical fibre, so the core is controlled rather than proven owned.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: Aryaka has built a dedicated security stack on top of our Software Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) architecture
sse_layer_ownership.note: NGFW-SWG, inline CASB, IPS, anti-malware, URL filtering, Secure Remote Access and Next-Gen DLP are Aryaka authored and run on the ANAP and on Aryaka's own POPs. Two partner exceptions exist and are add-ons rather than the core SSE stack: the SmartSecure Hosted VM Firewall Service uses Palo Alto Networks VM-Series, and the Services Description and Terms carries a Check Point EULA warranty disclaimer indicating a Check Point based managed firewall option.

regulatory_documentation.quote: maintains an SSAE-18 SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001:2013 certification
regulatory_documentation.note: Frameworks named on the Aryaka Trust Center: ISO/IEC 27001:2013 (with a Statement of Applicability document), SSAE-18 SOC 2 Type II, CSA STAR and CAIQ, GDPR and CCPA. Not found anywhere in the sources reviewed: NHS DSPT, DORA, NIS2, PCI DSS. The trust centre gates the underlying reports behind NDA request, so the quote is the attestation line rendered on the public landing page. Confidence is medium because the SafeBase page renders dynamically and wording may differ on re-fetch.

pop_count.quote: a global private network interconnected in a mesh service fabric of over 40 Points of Presence (PoPs) across the globe
pop_count.note: Aryaka publishes "over 40" and the managed Unified SASE page repeats "40+ PoPs". The PoP locations page enumerates roughly 47 individual city locations across Americas, EMEA and APAC and states they are located on all six habitable continents, without giving a headline figure, so the published headline number is 40+ rather than an exact count.

sla_availability_pct.quote: Global SLAs: Uptime of 99.999% on Day 1
sla_availability_pct.note: 99.999% is the headline availability commitment and appears repeatedly in the SLA document as "Uptime of 99.999%" for PrivateCore services, NGFW-SWG, PrivateAccess and RemoteUser gateways and Internet Breakout. A lower 99.99% figure applies to certain site pair scenarios, so the number varies by service element rather than being a single blanket figure.

sectors.healthcare.quote: Augmedix was named the number one most innovative healthcare company of 2016 by Fast Company.
sectors.healthcare.note: Weak and stale. The only healthcare-linked customer found anywhere on the site is Augmedix, and it is a healthcare technology vendor rather than a care provider or payer. Both press releases date from 2016. Healthcare does not appear in Aryaka's own published 'By Industries' filter on the resources index (source 18), there is no healthcare industry page alongside the three that do exist, and no HIPAA or HITRUST claim was found. I checked the three industry pages, the customers and proven-success pages, the resources industry filter and a site-scoped search for healthcare.

sectors.financial_services.note: Graded yes on a named customer (Calypso, a capital markets software firm) presented by Aryaka explicitly as a financial services company, plus 'Banking/Financial Services' being one of only six labels in Aryaka's own published industry filter. Confidence is medium not high because the evidence is an undated video testimonial rather than a written case study, there is no dedicated financial services industry page to sit alongside manufacturing, transport and professional services, and no banking accreditation or regulatory framework was found.

sectors.retail_ecommerce.quote: Aryaka Enables the Future of the Retail Customer Experience
sectors.retail_ecommerce.note: Retail is one of the six labels in Aryaka's own published industry filter and there is a retail-specific whitepaper, so this is more than a passing mention. It stops short of yes because no retailer is named anywhere, there is no retail case study, and there is no dedicated retail industry page. I checked the industry pages, customers page, resources industry filter and the retail whitepaper landing page.

sectors.manufacturing.note: The strongest sector by a distance. A dedicated industry page plus at least five named manufacturing customers with published case studies: Albemarle (Fortune 1000 chemicals), Hubbell, Thetford, AL-KO and Wabtec, with Lauridsen Group International also cited as a global manufacturer. The manufacturing page carries the case study line 'Hubbell Supercharges Global Application Performance, Visibility and Security'.

sectors.energy_utilities.quote: Discover how a Fortune 500 energy company enabled secure hybrid work and reduced network TCO.
sectors.energy_utilities.note: Graded yes on a named case study: World Fuel Services, now World Kinect, whose case study company profile block states Industry: Energy with roughly 4,700 employees and 75+ global sites. 'Energy' is also one of the six labels in Aryaka's published industry filter. Important qualification: this is fuel distribution and logistics, not a regulated utility, and Aryaka surfaces the customer under its Transportation & Logistics industry page rather than an energy page. No utility, grid, water or OT/SCADA evidence was found, so do not read this as utilities capability.

sectors.government_public_sector.quote: Customers span manufacturing, transportation, logistics, financial services, and business & professional services industries with complex multi-site, multi-cloud network requirements.
sectors.government_public_sector.note: No public sector evidence found. Government is absent from Aryaka's own six-label published industry filter and from the sentence quoted here. I checked the three industry pages, the customers and proven-success pages, the resources industry filter, and site-scoped searches for public sector, government and FedRAMP, which returned only unrelated partner and threat-research pages. No FedRAMP, StateRAMP, G-Cloud or comparable framework listing was found. Note that the Kleinfelder case study says that customer serves the public sector, but that describes Kleinfelder's own clients, not Aryaka's, and must not be read across.

sectors.education.quote: Customers span manufacturing, transportation, logistics, financial services, and business & professional services industries with complex multi-site, multi-cloud network requirements.
sectors.education.note: No education evidence found. Education is absent from Aryaka's published industry filter. A site-scoped search surfaced only a 2020 blog about coronavirus, universities and remote access, which is commentary on the sector with no named institution, no case study and no customer, so it does not even support partial. I checked the industry pages, customers page, resources industry filter and case study index.

sectors.transport_logistics.quote: Trusted by Leading Transportation & Logistics Companies
sectors.transport_logistics.note: Dedicated industry page headed 'Secure, Simplify, and Scale Transportation & Logistics Networks' with named customers Cathay Pacific (166 branch sites, deployment corroborated by a dated press release and by PR Newswire and Intelligent CIO APAC coverage seen in search), Wabtec (rail, 50+ locations) and World Fuel Services. Transportation & Logistics is also one of the six labels in the published industry filter.

sectors.professional_services.quote: Unified SASE as a Service: For Business & Professional Services
sectors.professional_services.note: Dedicated industry page plus one named case study, Kleinfelder, a multi-disciplinary engineering consultancy of 3,100 staff across 100+ locations in North America and Australia. 'Business Services' is one of the six labels in the published industry filter. Slightly thinner on named customers than manufacturing or transport, resting on a single logo.

sectors.hospitality_leisure.quote: Customers span manufacturing, transportation, logistics, financial services, and business & professional services industries with complex multi-site, multi-cloud network requirements.
sectors.hospitality_leisure.note: No hospitality or leisure evidence found. The sector is absent from Aryaka's published industry filter and from the customer-span sentence quoted here. I checked the industry pages, customers and proven-success pages, resources industry filter, and a site-scoped search for hotel, hospitality and restaurant, which returned only unrelated award and analyst-recognition pages. Cathay Pacific is an airline and is presented as transport, not leisure, so it must not be counted here.

regions.uk_ireland.note: Aryaka publishes named PoP locations in both the UK and Ireland. The same EMEA list on the PoP page carries 'London, England' alongside the Dublin entry quoted here, and the global connectivity datasheet independently repeats London and Dublin in its EMEA grouping. This is service delivery infrastructure, not a sales office. The PoP page is undated so the list currency is unconfirmed.

regions.europe.note: Continental European PoPs published on the EMEA list: Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Paris, Madrid and Stockholm. Corroborated by the same five appearing in the datasheet EMEA grouping. Coverage is western and northern Europe; no central or eastern European PoP is listed.

regions.north_america.note: The densest region in the published estate. The Americas list carries ten US PoPs (Ashburn, Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, Newark, San Jose, Seattle) plus the Toronto entry quoted here, and the company is headquartered in Santa Clara. No Mexico PoP is listed.

regions.asia_pacific.note: Extensive published APAC estate: Sydney, Melbourne, Tokyo, Seoul, Taipei, Ho Chi Minh City, Hong Kong, Singapore and four Indian PoPs (Bangalore, Chennai, Delhi, Mumbai). Backed by delivery evidence rather than PoPs alone, in the Cathay Pacific deployment out of Hong Kong. Mainland China is graded separately below.

regions.middle_east_africa.note: Published PoPs at Johannesburg, Dubai and Tel Aviv within the EMEA list, corroborated by the datasheet. Confidence is medium rather than high because coverage is three cities for the whole of the Middle East and Africa, with nothing in west, east or north Africa, and no MEA customer or case study was found to demonstrate delivery.

regions.latin_america.note: Meets the published-PoP test, but only just. The Americas list contains exactly two Latin American entries, the Sao Paulo entry quoted here and 'Santiago de Chile'. No Mexico, Colombia or Argentina PoP is listed and no Latin American customer or case study was found. Aryaka does not itself describe this coverage as limited, which is why it is graded yes rather than partial, but a buyer with Latin American sites should verify reach beyond Brazil and Chile.

regions.china_mainland.quote: We have strategic partnerships with leading Chinese data-center and telecom providers Alibaba, IDCBC and Infoquick to operate our in country PoPs for ensuring full compliance with all privacy and data security laws and regulations.
regions.china_mainland.note: This is the specific licensed arrangement the brief asks for, not a generic global claim. Aryaka publishes named mainland PoPs (Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, plus Hong Kong) and states explicitly that those in-country PoPs are operated by named Chinese partners for regulatory compliance, which is why the grade is partner_integrated rather than yes. Aryaka's China experience is also cited as a selection factor in the dated Cathay press release. The older ChinaNetCloud reseller release shows the same partner-led model historically but is undated on the page and names a different partner, so it is background only, not a conflict to resolve.

organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.quote: Cathay was looking for an agile provider that could deliver a flexible, cost-effective, high-performance SD-WAN network along with security at the edge to support its organization across more than 150 locations.
organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.note: Clearly the primary target. Evidenced by case studies rather than positioning alone: Cathay Pacific at 166 branch sites, Albemarle as a Fortune 1000 company with over 5,000 staff operating in more than 100 countries, Wabtec at 29,000 employees across 50+ locations, and World Kinect across 75+ global sites. The products and services page describes 'AI-powered solutions tailored for global enterprises.'

organisation_fit.mid_market.quote: Managing a network in a mid-sized company is tough.
organisation_fit.mid_market.note: Aryaka runs a dedicated mid-market landing page using 'mid-market enterprises', 'mid-sized enterprises' and 'mid-sized company' throughout, and has a matching customer in AL-KO, described as a global German medium-sized company of roughly 700 employees across 19 locations. The sase-reviews page also carries a 'Head of Infrastructure, Mid-Market' reviewer label. Confidence is medium because Aryaka publishes no employee or revenue band defining what it means by mid-market, so the boundary against its enterprise segment is unstated.

organisation_fit.small_business.quote: Research shows that the three main networking and security challenges that small to medium-sized companies face are limited budgets, lack of skilled IT resources, and the need for operational simplicity.
organisation_fit.small_business.note: Graded partial, not yes. Aryaka has published an explicitly SME-aimed offering with a stated entry price and a three-tier package structure, which is real targeting, but the language is consistently 'small to medium-sized enterprises' and the accompanying case studies start at roughly 700 employees. No customer, case study or self-service tier at genuine small-business scale was found, and the SME blog is undated so the offer's current status is unconfirmed. A per-site price of 150 US dollars per month also implies a multi-site business rather than a single-site small company.

published_pricing.quote: Our entry price begins at $150 per site/per month.
published_pricing.note: Unusually for this market, Aryaka does publish a hard entry point. The quoted string was re-verified on a second fetch together with its surrounding paragraph. Graded mid rather than budget or premium: 150 US dollars per site per month is an entry figure for a fully managed service that includes a global private backbone, application optimisation and lifecycle management, and it scales up through three published tiers (SD-WAN, then Unified SASE, then Advanced Security) plus add-ons, so realised cost for a typical buyer will sit above the entry point. Aryaka's own positioning pulls in two directions and I have not resolved it: the SME blog frames the service as affordable while the pricing and packaging material frames it as an enterprise-grade managed service with 'transparent, predictable pricing'. Caveats: the entry price sits in an undated blog rather than a rate card, no per-tier figures are published anywhere, and TrustRadius (source 32) confirms no pricing plans are listed on the main marketplace aggregator. A buyer should treat the figure as indicative only.
